For this, I would need to escalate your case to our special care team. Our team will get in touch with you within the next 2-3 working days to discuss the specific options and required documents. Please keep those ready. transcript: Agent:"Hello, am I speaking with Mrs. Priya Sharma?"Customer:"Yes, this is Priya. Who is calling, please?"Agent:"Good morning, Mrs. Sharma. My name is Sameer from Bharat Finance. I am calling regarding your outstanding EMI payment for loan account number BFH012345. Your EMI of fifteen thousand five hundred rupees was due on the 28th of last month, and we haven't received it yet."Customer:"Oh, yes, I am aware of it, Sameer. Thank you for calling. I was actually about to call your team myself."Agent:"Alright, Mrs. Sharma. Is there any particular reason for the delay? We understand sometimes there might be unexpected issues, but it's important to clear the outstanding amount as soon as possible to avoid further late payment charges."Customer:"Yes, there is an issue, but it's not that I don't want to pay. My bank account, from which the EMI usually gets debited, has been put on hold. It's my savings account with National Bank."Agent:"On hold? Could you please elaborate, Mrs. Sharma? What is the reason for your account being on hold?"Customer:"Yes, the bank says there's some KYC document pending on my side. I had some old account details, and they want me to update my Aadhaar and PAN again. I've submitted the documents, but it takes a few days for them to process it. So right now, I cannot access funds or make any transactions from that account. Everything is stuck."Agent:"I understand, Mrs. Sharma. So, because of the bank's KYC hold, you're unable to make the payment. Is that correct? Have you been given an estimate of when the hold might be lifted?"Customer:"That's correct. They said maybe two or three more days. But honestly, it's very frustrating. I have the funds, the money is there in the account, but I cannot use it. So my hands are tied until the bank releases it. And this EMI is the first thing I need to pay once it's open."Agent:"Understood, Mrs. Sharma. This is certainly an operational blockage. Are there any other alternative payment methods you could consider in the meantime? For example, do you have another bank account, or perhaps you could use a UPI payment if that account is not linked to the blocked one, or maybe even a direct transfer from a relative's account?"Customer:"Well, Sameer, most of my funds are tied up in that main account. I don't really have another account with significant balance right now. And regarding UPI, it's also linked to the same main account, so that's also blocked. Asking a relative would be a last resort, but I prefer to make the payment myself once my account is active again. It should only be a few days."Agent:"Okay, Mrs. Sharma, I note that your willingness to pay is clear, and the delay is due to an unavoidable bank-imposed account hold. We'll mark this reason in your file. What date do you anticipate the hold will be lifted, and you would be able to make the payment?"Customer:"Hmm, let's say by next Monday, the 10th of this month. I really hope it's resolved by then. I will definitely prioritize your EMI as soon as I get access."Agent:"Alright, Mrs. Sharma. I will schedule a follow-up call for next Monday evening, say around 6 PM, to check if the account is active and if you've been able to make the payment. Is that a convenient time?"Customer:"Yes, 6 PM on Monday is fine. I'll make sure to get this sorted by then. Thank you for understanding."Agent:"You're welcome, Mrs. Sharma. Just to reiterate, the outstanding amount is Rs. 15,500 plus any applicable late fees which we can discuss once your account is active. We look forward to hearing from you. Have a good day."Customer:"You too, Sameer. Goodbye."
